title: Performance term
description: One quantity in a performance record, carrying what evidence produced it, over what regime it is claimed, and whether it is known at all. UNKNOWN is a distinct inhabited state spelled as the string "UNKNOWN" -- NEVER as 0, null or a missing key, each of which a consumer can read as a number. A term whose value is "UNKNOWN" must carry unknown_reason. Implemented by merlin.perf.term.PerformanceTerm.

name.description: What this term quantifies, e.g. total_cycles / dma_busy_cycles / moved_bytes. Kept identical across targets so a target-vs-target diff is trivial.

value.description: The quantity, or the token "UNKNOWN". Booleans and null are rejected: a bool priced as 1 and a null read as 0 are both fabricated numbers.

unit.description: The unit the value is in (cycles, bytes, ratio, ...). Required: an unlabelled number is not a measurement.

provenance.description: Where the value came from. The kind vocabulary is merlin.dse_guidance.evidence.EVIDENCE_TYPES, strongest to weakest, shared with the DSE-guidance layer so confidence is one scale across the repo.

evidence.description: The specific things the value rests on: source ids declared in the record, files, derivations. Required and non-empty -- a term that names nothing cites nothing. Naming a source the record declares with role 'diagnostic' is rejected by merlin.perf.record.

confidence.description: Confidence WEIGHT, defaulted from the provenance kind (merlin.dse_guidance.evidence.confidence_for). A ranking weight, not an accuracy claim.

validity.description: The regime over which the value is claimed to hold. Field-shape-compatible with ModeLIR's mlc/validate/fidelity.py::FidelityContract so the two can be converted once enough real terms exist to say what the unified lattice is (the unification is deliberately deferred).

validated_regime.description: Where the value was actually established. Required: a value with no stated domain is a value claimed everywhere.

expected_error.description: The error to expect inside the validated regime.

weak_regime.description: Where the value is known to degrade, stated rather than discovered later.

escalate_when.description: The predicate under which this term must not be used and a stronger measurement is required.

bounds.description: Admissible range. Either end may be "UNKNOWN", which is NOT an infinity -- 'no bound was derived' must not read as 'the bound is infinite', because a comparison against infinity always passes.

unknown_reason.description: Why the value could not be established. REQUIRED when value is "UNKNOWN" and forbidden otherwise: 'not established' and 'nobody looked' demand different follow-up, and only the reason separates them.
